sources.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, revision 4
sources.evidence: Section 2.1 and Table 2.1 identify GPT-3 as the largest 175.0B model: 96 layers, width 12288, 96 attention heads of dimension 128, feed-forward width four times the hidden width, and a 2048-token context. The architecture follows GPT-2 with alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention. The table explicitly defines its count as total trainable parameters. The PDF was also downloaded and read.

sources.title: OpenAI API launch
sources.evidence: Dated June 11, 2020. Launches a private beta with access requests and text-in/text-out completion using weights from the GPT-3 family. Explains choosing controlled API access instead of open-sourcing the models. It does not enumerate dated endpoint IDs or explicitly name the 175B checkpoint in the launch body.

sources.title: GPT-3 Model Card, September 2020
sources.evidence: Explicitly describes the 175B autoregressive Transformer and controlled commercial/scientific access through OpenAI API terms. Confirms text data and generation. Distinguishes the original May 2020 model from a September retraining, so the card date and later training cutoff are not transferred to this original release.

sources.title: OpenAI licenses GPT-3 technology to Microsoft
sources.evidence: September 22, 2020 announcement recalls the June API launch and identifies GPT-3 as the 175B model offered through it. Describes a commercial license to Microsoft while continued OpenAI API access remains available. Supports proprietary hosted distribution and the historical API relationship, not a byte-identical June endpoint mapping.

sources.title: Language models are few-shot learners
sources.evidence: The May 28, 2020 research announcement identifies the original GPT-3 model, its published 175B count and text-based few-shot evaluation. This is the paper announcement, preceding the June API private beta.

sources.title: Aligning language models to follow instructions
sources.evidence: January 2022 comparison explicitly labels its baseline 175B GPT-3 and explains that InstructGPT models are later human-feedback fine-tunes. It corroborates the nominal size but does not provide an original-checkpoint census or separately defined active count. Later instruction tuning is not attributed to the original GPT-3 model.

sources.title: More Efficient In-Context Learning with GLaM
sources.publisher: Google Research, Andrew M. Dai and Nan Du
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. The December 9, 2021 Results table explicitly identifies GPT-3 (175B) and reports Total Parameters 0.175T and Activated Parameters 0.175T. The post links the original Brown et al. GPT-3 paper. This is Google Research's nominal comparison convention, not an OpenAI active-count disclosure.

sources.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts, ICML 2022
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened and Table 2 visually checked on PDF page 3, October 27, 2026. The table defines total trainable parameters and activated model parameters per input token, then lists GPT-3 as a dense decoder-only model with 175B in both columns. The introduction and reference identify Brown et al. (2020), Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, establishing the original GPT-3 identity. The count is the Google authors' published nominal comparison convention, without an exact component census.

name.note: The paper explicitly labels the largest model GPT-3 175B or GPT-3.

developer.note: The original paper, announcement and model card identify OpenAI.

family.note: This record represents the largest original GPT-3 model, not a later InstructGPT fine-tune.

release_date.note: Retain the record's defined milestone: the initial OpenAI API private-beta announcement and opening of access requests. The launch names GPT-3-family weights; the later first-party post binds the 175B model to that API. This is not a public-weight release, general availability, or proof of an immutable 175B endpoint version on that date. The research announcement was May 28.

open_weights.note: The original release provided controlled hosted access instead of public model weights. The repository releases evidence and samples, not the checkpoint.

license.note: Descriptive classification of a controlled commercial API model and separately licensed technology. It is not an open-weight license name or a reconstruction of historical contract wording.

parameters_b.note: Freshly rechecked original Table 2.1: GPT-3 175B or GPT-3 is reported at 175.0B total trainable parameters. Preserve OpenAI's nominal total; Google's GLaM comparison also reports 175B. Neither source establishes an exact integer tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Google's original GLaM paper Table 2 explicitly reports 175B activated model parameters per input token for the original GPT-3, citing Brown et al. (2020); its release blog also tabulates 0.175T activated. Adopt that nominal Google comparison convention, not an OpenAI disclosure or an exact tensor-participation claim. This is not inferred from dense architecture or the GPT-3 Appendix D training-FLOP assumptions.

architecture.note: The original GPT-2-style decoder has dense learned projections and feed-forward layers: 96 layers, width 12288, 96 heads and feed-forward width 49152. Alternating dense/local sparse attention describes token connectivity, not expert routing or MoE weights.

context_window.note: Section 2.1 explicitly gives a 2048-token context for every model in the table, including GPT-3 175B. The few-shot evaluation section uses that same full context. This is the original model limit, not a later API variant's limit.

modalities.note: Original model and API use tokenized text prompts and generated text completions; the card does not describe image, audio or video inputs or outputs.

reasoning.note: Commonsense reasoning and arithmetic evaluations do not establish a dedicated reasoning mode. No such feature specification or explicit incapability statement is provided for this original model.

tool_call.note: The documented interface is text completion. No native structured tool-call protocol is specified for the original GPT-3 model; absence of a protocol does not prove categorical inability.

description.value: Largest original GPT-3 model, a 96-layer Transformer for text completion and learning from examples in its prompt.
description.note: The paper documents the largest original model's depth, autoregressive text generation and few-shot prompting without gradient updates.

patch.description: Largest original GPT-3 model, a 96-layer Transformer for text completion and learning from examples in its prompt.
patch.notes: June 11, 2020 marks the initial API private-beta announcement and access requests; the paper was announced May 28. OpenAI reports a nominal 175B total; Google's GLaM comparison reports a nominal 175B activated per input token. The original model has a 2048-token context and alternating dense/local sparse attention. The September 2020 retraining and later InstructGPT models are distinct versions.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit retains OpenAI's nominal 175B total and establishes nominal 175B active using Google's explicit GLaM comparison table for the original GPT-3. Attribution and counting precision remain explicit; this is not an exact tensor census or OpenAI active-count disclosure. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged, including the API private-beta milestone, context, architecture and unresolved reasoning/tool-call claims.
